# Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, read https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

Domain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.

**If `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` and the task is site-specific, read every file in the matching `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<site>/` directory before inventing an approach.**

## Usage

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

- Invoke as `browser-use`. Use heredocs for multi-line commands.
- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.
- First navigation for a task is `new_tab(url)`, not `goto_url(url)`. The daemon
  preserves the attached tab across separate CLI invocations, so do not call
  `new_tab()` again in every script.
- Keep one working tab per task/site. Before opening another, inspect
  `current_tab()` and `list_tabs()` and use `switch_tab()` to reuse a matching
  tab. Do not leave duplicate tabs on the same URL or close tabs you did not
  create.
- At task completion, close tabs created for the task that are no longer needed.
  Keep a tab open if the user needs to see it, it is needed for a known follow-up,
  or closing it could discard unsaved work or other important state.
- `new_tab()` and `switch_tab()` attach and move the horse marker without
  changing Chrome's visible tab. Screenshots and normal CDP input work in the
  background. Never call `activate_tab(target)` automatically: it brings Chrome
  to the foreground. Call it only when the user explicitly asks to see or
  visibly switch to that tab. Do not pair `switch_tab()` with `activate_tab()`.
- A local daemon is a connection to the whole Chrome instance, not to one site,
  task, card, or agent. Omit `BU_NAME` and reuse the default daemon for normal
  sequential local work across websites, tabs, screenshots, and Codex turns.
  Do not invent per-job names such as `gmail1375` or `slack1371`: every new
  local daemon opens another browser-level CDP connection and Chrome may show
  another Allow prompt.
- Set `BH_TAB_MARKER=0` before starting the daemon to leave page titles unchanged.
  The horse marker remains enabled by default.
- A timeout or page that pauses while hidden is not permission to foreground
  Chrome. Keep using background CDP operations. For a focus-gated page,
  temporarily call `cdp("Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled", enabled=True)`,
  perform and verify the operation, then disable it in a `finally` block. If
  background control still cannot work, report that limitation instead of
  activating the tab. Do not invent a `Runtime.evaluate` scroll replacement or
  a cross-frame JS walker.
- The normal local flow attaches to the running Chrome/Chromium CDP endpoint. No browser ids or local profile selection.

## plugin:desktop-commander:desktop-commander
Desktop Commander provides tools for working with the user's authorized device.
- Filesystem tools handle direct file and directory operations within configured access boundaries.
- Terminal process tools support shell commands, REPLs, and long-running processes. start_process creates a process session; interact_with_process sends input; read_process_output reads later output; force_terminate ends a session.
- Search tools are session-based. start_search creates a search session; get_more_search_results reads its results; stop_search ends it early.
- Absolute paths are generally the most reliable because relative paths depend on the active working directory.
- allowedDirectories and each tool's schema, annotations, and documented constraints define the operational boundaries.

- The 8 GDD sections are: Overview, Player Fantasy, Detailed Rules, Formulas, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Tuning Knobs, Acceptance Criteria
- **How many are required depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system **defines numeric rules**: rates, curves, thresholds, costs, damage, drop weights — anything a balance pass would tune) at `standard`, none at `minimal` (the design record there is `design/game-brief.md`). Resolve the tier before flagging a section as missing; see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`
- **The Formulas test is what the system defines, not what it is called.** A system's `Category` in `systems-index.md` is a hint — `Gameplay`, `Economy` and `Progression` almost always qualify — never the test. Do not gate Formulas on a category token: the categories `/map-systems` writes (`Core · Gameplay · Progression · Economy · Persistence · UI · Audio · Narrative · Meta`) do not include `combat` or `AI`, which are example systems *within* `Gameplay`. Every site stating this rule must state the same test.
- **Section-name alias**: The GDD template and `/design-system` author this section as `## Detailed Design`; the design standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. These are the SAME required section — accept either heading and never rewrite one into the other.
- Formulas must include variable definitions, expected value ranges, and example calculations
- Edge cases must explicitly state what happens, not just "handle gracefully"
- Dependencies must be bidirectional — if system A depends on B, B's doc must mention A
- Tuning knobs must specify safe ranges and what gameplay aspect they affect
- Acceptance criteria must be testable — a QA tester must be able to verify pass/fail
- No hand-waving: "the system should feel good" is not a valid specification
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale
- Design documents MUST be written incrementally: create skeleton first, then fill
  each section one at a time with user approval between sections. Write each
  approved section to the file immediately to persist decisions and manage context

# Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## GDD Files (`design/gdd/`)

The 8 GDD sections, in order:
1. Overview — one-paragraph summary
2. Player Fantasy — intended feeling and experience
3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

**How many are REQUIRED depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`; 5 at
`standard` (Overview, Detailed Rules, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Acceptance
Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where
`design/game-brief.md` is the design record instead of a GDD. Resolve the tier
before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> **Three other places already encode the tier rule** —
> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
> `.claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh`. This file is the copy a session working in
> `design/` reads first, so it must agree with them: demanding all 8 at
> `minimal` warns a jam project about six sections its own configuration says it
> does not need, which trains the user to ignore the warning.

**Section-name alias:** the GDD template and `/design-system` author section 3
as `## Detailed Design`; the standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. Same required
section — accept either heading, never rewrite one into the other.

**File naming:** `[system-slug].md` (e.g. `movement-system.md`, `combat-system.md`)

**Systems index:** `design/gdd/systems-index.md` — update when adding a new GDD.

**Design order:** Foundation → Core → Feature → Presentation → Polish

**Validation:** Run `/design-review [path]` after authoring any GDD.
Run `/review-all-gdds` after completing a set of related GDDs.

## Quick Specs (`design/quick-specs/`)

Lightweight specs for tuning changes, minor mechanics, or balance adjustments.
Use `/quick-design` to author.

## UX Specs (`design/ux/`)

- Per-screen specs: `design/ux/[screen-name].md`
- HUD design: `design/ux/hud.md`
- Interaction pattern library: `design/ux/interaction-patterns.md`
- Accessibility requirements: `design/accessibility-requirements.md`

Use `/ux-design` to author. Validate with `/ux-review` before passing to `/team-ui`.

> **Accessibility requirements sit OUTSIDE `design/ux/` on purpose.** They are a
> project-wide standard the per-screen specs consult, not a spec for one screen.
> `.claude/docs/workflow-catalog.yaml`, the Pre-Production, Production and Polish
> gates, and `/architecture-review` all check `design/accessibility-requirements.md`
> at that exact path. Do not "tidy" it under `design/ux/` — every one of those
> checks would stop matching, and the Technical Setup → Pre-Production gate would
> become unpassable. `/ux-design` states the same rule at its `accessibility` mode.

Two sparse tables: `bodies` keyed by `body_id` (Layout's id) and `actors` keyed by `actor_id`, plus the block-local counter `next_actor_id` (CR-8: entity ids are allocated by the owning block from a counter stored inside it). Body repeats what Layout asked it to repeat (LY-18): it owns `body.state` (pose, velocity, actor positions); its `restore_after` is `[layout.state]`; and it owns the physics `PROJECTOR` slot (BDY-33). *Rejected:* `PER_PLAYER` scope (bodies and pods have no PlayerId); two blocks (`body.state` and `body.frames`) — a second restore node and a second owner registration where EM-1 names one. *Decides:* R2, EM-1, SL:288; CR-8. (auto: registration lint) → ADR-BODY-02.

136	**BDY-6 — One position name.** The persisted canonical field is **`pos_curr`** (the name EM:426, LO:217 and SL:474 already read). `pos_prev` is DERIVED: set `:= pos_curr` in `post_restore`, at placement and at every transfer, never persisted. The Controller's `pos` (PCI:447, "`body.state.pos`") is an alias for `pos_curr`; this sentence is where the alias is declared, once (a wording note is routed to Save/Load, whose SL:474 and SL:849 list both `pos` and `pos_curr`, and to the Controller). `blocked` and every `diag` value are derived and outside the hashed set. *Decides:* R2, R3, PIPE C5, SL-15 item 8 (SL:230). 138	**BDY-7 — Persisted fields (schema v1).** Per actor: `{actor_id, kind, seat, body_id, pos_curr (x, y), sub (x, y), last_octant, odometer}`. Per body, sparse (a row absent means all zeros): `{body_id, world_x, world_y, vel_x, vel_y, heading_q}`. Block scalar: `next_actor_id`. `last_octant` (0-7, 8 = NONE) is **Body's own** record of the octant its last step integrated; it is a different field from `controller.state`'s decel-ladder memory of the same name (PCI:311), and this sentence is the disambiguation. `seat` is the PlayerId whose `controller.state` row feeds this actor's intent; **seat 0 means "no seat" (`AGENT` rows; any number of `AGENT` rows may carry it) and PlayerIds start at 1; two `SEAT` rows may never share a seat, and a `SEAT` row with `seat` 0 or a negative seat is `BDY_PLACE_BAD_KIND` at placement and `BDY_RESTORE_KIND` on restore** (the kernel defines a PlayerId as "a stable seat identity (1 in single-player)", KRN:52, and Suit keys by an integer PlayerId, SE-2; no designed GDD assigns PlayerId 0, and the kernel states the reservation once, KRN:52, answered *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*); it is persisted because the kernel's binding table "is not saved, since sessions rebuild it" (KRN:100), so after a restore nothing else says which `actor_id` is seat 1; Body matches an actor to its Controller row on its own `seat` field, so no kernel reverse lookup is needed. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Who rebuilds the kernel's `PlayerId → {controlled entity IDs}` binding after a load (the step KRN:100 leaves unowned).** KRN:100 says the table "may be rebuilt from Body's `seat` field" and SL-20 says "a session rebuilds it", but no GDD assigns the step, and the MVP death-restart path (restore the last autosave, then play) needs it: without it a seat-1 command fails the authority stage (`ACTOR_NOT_OWNED`, KRN CR-5) after every restore. Body's half of the contract is stated here and is closed: Body publishes the pure read `seat_bindings() -> [(seat, actor_id)]` (ascending `seat`, `SEAT` rows only, derived from the actors table on each call, no persisted field) and nothing else. The other half is **the session owner's control-plane step (KRN CR-15, host-only binding API, honoured at P6 per CR-14), run once after the last `post_restore()` of `LOADING` and before the first `RUNNING` tick, which clears the table and re-binds each `seat` in `seat_bindings()` to its `actor_id`**; that half is the kernel's and Save/Load's to record and is routed (8.3, Open Question 30), not decided here. AC-BDY-6 is therefore an integration criterion through the real load path, tagged BLOCKED-ON the kernel and Save/Load rows until they record the step. A `SEAT` row with no Controller row (a Vertical Slice disconnect, a corrupt save) is **not stepped**, is treated as `v_eff` 0 (`sub` and `last_octant` reset) and is counted `BDY_SEAT_UNBOUND`. `odometer` is 64-bit and travels in the binary payload (SL-2), never as a JSON number. *(orchestrator ruling: `seat` is an additive field beyond R3's list, adopted from the technical-director and engine-programmer proposals, which independently found the gap; the engine-programmer's name `owner_ref` is dropped in favour of the kernel's vocabulary, CR-7.)* *Decides:* R2, R3, CR-7, CR-8. Doors still respect every actor: `leaf_would_overlap` takes every seat's foot box (LY-11, BDY-18), so "a door will not close on any crewmate" still holds. Crowding in a one-tile corridor at four seats is a Vertical Slice question (Open Questions). *Decides:* PCI:105, PCI:139; P2; anti-pillar "no intentional PvP". (auto)

178	**BDY-20 — Actor lifecycle: place, remove, capacity.** BM1 `place_actor(body_id, pos, kind, seat) -> actor_id` **allocates** the id from `next_actor_id` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: BM1 returns that `actor_id` (>= 1) or a negative `FAULT_CODE`, and a fault writes nothing and leaves `next_actor_id` unchanged, BDY-21)* (first id 1, never reused after a removal, int64) and writes the row with `pos_prev := pos_curr`, `sub := (0, 0)`, `last_octant := 8`, `odometer := 0`. 180	**BDY-21 — Mutator surface BM1-BM7, all Class A; every mutator returns OK or a FAULT_CODE; validation is a pure read.** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the contract of this rule is rewritten; the earlier assumption that an apply cannot fail is struck, because it contradicted MSA-14, MSA-31 and AC-MSA-142)* Body publishes seven mutators — BM1 `place_actor`, BM2 `remove_actor`, BM3 `rebase_on_attach`, BM4 `rebase_on_detach`, BM5 `transfer_actor`, BM6 `set_body_velocity`, BM7 `set_body_pose` (added at the consistency pass 2026-10-27, routed from `web-map-and-transit.md` ASK-B1, WM-6) — each called only from Assembly's or Transit's single `apply`, AFTER the Layout mutator in the same `WriteScope` (KRN:197 names the three mutator owners; the order inside one scope, Graph then Layout then Body, is Assembly's contract (Modular Ship Assembly is Designed and repeats it: MSA-14, table T3 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*), implied by Layout returning the records Body consumes, LY-16, LY-17). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **Every mutator returns a status; none is assumed to succeed.** GDScript has no throw and no catch, and `assert()` is compiled out of a release export, so a mutator that cannot honour its apply-time predicate has to say so in its return value (the caller's half is MSA-31, MSA-14 and AC-MSA-142). BM2 to BM7 return an `int`: `OK` (0) or a NEGATIVE `FAULT_CODE`, which is the negated Body reason constant of the `can_*` read that would have rejected the call (reason constants are positive ints, so `-BDY_PLACE_CAPACITY` is a `FAULT_CODE`). BM1 returns the allocated `actor_id` (an int >= 1) or a negative `FAULT_CODE`: one return channel, no out-parameter and no per-call allocation. `rc < 0` is a fault for every mutator. The caller's `apply` (Assembly's or Transit's) checks the status after EVERY Body call and, on the first negative value, calls the kernel's fault entry (MSA-31, ASK K2) and makes no further mutator call, so a failure inside `apply` moves the kernel to `FAULTED` (KRN:104). Body's mutators are not kernel-registered owner callables (they run inside the caller's `apply`); Body's kernel-registered callables (`body.integrate`, `snapshot`, `restore`, `post_restore`) take the kernel's `ctx`, return their results through it and end `return ctx.complete()` (delegated ruling R3). What R8 calls "BM1 validates ..." is **published as pure `can_*` precondition reads** — `can_place`, `can_remove`, `can_rebase_attach`, `can_rebase_detach`, `can_transfer`, `can_set_velocity`, `can_set_pose` — that the caller's `validate` invokes before any mutator runs, exactly as the Graph's pure `can_join` serves weld validation; inside `apply` the same checks are re-evaluated as the apply-time predicate below, and every mutator is **check-then-write** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: it evaluates its WHOLE predicate before its first row write, so a call that returns a `FAULT_CODE` has written nothing (the tables, `next_actor_id`, the dirty set and the event queue are exactly as before the call, and no half-applied weld or cut exists). Every apply-time defect calls the injectable **`plan_mismatch_sink`**, a module-level `Callable` taking `(mutator_id, code)`: its default increments the counter `BDY_PLAN_MISMATCH`, which is ACTIVE in every build, and in a debug build also calls `push_error`. No mutator path uses `assert()`, because a GDScript `assert` is compiled out of release and cannot be intercepted by a test; a test injects a recording sink and exercises every defect in the ordinary debug gdUnit4 runner (harness rule 1). The apply-time predicate per mutator is a mismatch with the pre-state its `can_*` read would have proven: BM1 any `can_place` reason; BM2 an unknown actor; BM3 the two ids equal or the surviving body not live in Layout; BM4 the old body not live, `new_body_id` not live in Layout, or a `moved_sections[]` member not owned by `new_body_id` (the call-order trap of BDY-23), or *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* a new pose row out of range *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: this one is NOT a failing predicate; it is the saturate-and-continue branch of the split below)*; BM5 an unknown actor, an unknown destination or an arrival box inside a SOLID rectangle; BM6 an unknown body or a velocity out of range; BM7 an unknown body or a coordinate out of range. **The split per defect class *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.** (i) *Return-the-code class* (the call writes nothing and returns the `FAULT_CODE`; the caller faults the kernel): an unknown, equal or dead id (BM2 `BDY_UNKNOWN_ACTOR`; BM3 and BM4 `BDY_REBASE_SAME_BODY` or `BDY_REBASE_UNKNOWN_BODY`; BM5 `BDY_UNKNOWN_ACTOR` or `BDY_PLACE_UNKNOWN_BODY`; BM6 `BDY_VEL_UNKNOWN_BODY`; BM7 `BDY_POSE_UNKNOWN_BODY`); a BM4 `moved_sections[]` member not owned by `new_body_id` (`BDY_REBASE_SECTION_NOT_OWNED`, the call-order trap of BDY-23); a BM3 or BM4 `frame_shift_px` off Layout's 24-px grid (`BDY_REBASE_SHIFT_OFF_GRID`); any rejected BM1, including an over-cap one (`BDY_PLACE_CAPACITY` and the other `can_place` reasons); a BM5 arrival box inside a SOLID rectangle (`BDY_PLACE_INSIDE_FOOTPRINT`); a BM6 velocity or BM7 coordinate out of range (`BDY_VEL_OUT_OF_RANGE`, `BDY_POSE_OUT_OF_RANGE`; the call writes nothing, so no unloadable row can result). (ii) *Saturate-and-continue class* (the call completes and returns `OK`): **only BM4's new pose row**, where `world_old + frame_shift_px` leaves `±WORLD_COORD_LIMIT` or `vel_old` plus drift leaves `±VEL_MAX_PX_PER_TICK`; it saturates per BDY-23, the sink counts `BDY_WORLD_LIMIT` (where applicable) and `BDY_PLAN_MISMATCH`, and BM4 returns `OK`. The reason is the user's ruling that a death restarts from the last autosave: by the time BM4 runs the Graph and Layout have already applied the cut, and a row `restore` would reject (`BDY_RESTORE_POSE_RANGE`) would make the next autosave unloadable, so this branch is load-bearing and must not become a fault. Class (i) is checked first: a BM4 call that has both an unknown new body and a range overflow returns the code. *Consistency* after any call, including every call that returned a `FAULT_CODE`: `restore(snapshot())` accepts the block, actor ids are unique and below `next_actor_id`, and every `body_id` in either table is live in Layout; there is no exception (an over-cap BM1 is a returned code and writes no row, so no over-cap row can exist and Open Question 13 is closed). This *is* validate-then-apply (CR-9) with the two halves held by different owners. None of the `can_*` reads needs Layout's apply-time return record *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: except that `can_rebase_detach` takes the seam's `frame_shift_px` as a caller-supplied argument, below, exactly as `docked` does)*: each proves only that the bodies it names are live in Layout's pre-state, that ids differ and, for BM4, that the new pose row is in range (`can_rebase_detach(old_body_id, frame_shift_px)` proves that the old body is live in Layout *and, (Amended 2026-10-27 — design review), that the cut cannot produce a pose row `restore` would reject*: it answers `BDY_REBASE_POSE_OUT_OF_RANGE` when `world_old + frame_shift_px` leaves `±WORLD_COORD_LIMIT` on either axis and `BDY_VEL_OUT_OF_RANGE` when `vel_old` plus the drift (BDY-28) leaves `±VEL_MAX_PX_PER_TICK`; `frame_shift_px` is the value Layout's D.12 fixes for the seam (Assembly passes its own V3 `frame_shift_px`, the value its `detach_preview` produced, to this read, so the range guard runs on the real validate path; the Layout preview itself is optional, Open Question 34; Assembly's V4 row and AC-MSA-77 still show the one-argument form, which Assembly conforms to this signature because the registry's `body_mutators` is sourced here (G1); at apply time Layout's REAL record is authoritative as for every other mutator) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; a fresh Layout `body_id` cannot already own a Body row, because `BDY_RESTORE_UNKNOWN_BODY` rejects any Body id Layout does not hold, and an apply-time disagreement between a returned record and the pre-state returns its `FAULT_CODE` and is reported to the sink as `BDY_PLAN_MISMATCH`); at `apply` time Assembly passes Layout's REAL record, which Body treats as authoritative. Body registers no player command type and subscribes to no Layout dirty keys. *Rejected:* Body reconciling from Layout's dirty keys inside its hook (a write outside a mutator; CR-9), and Layout calling Body (breaks the acyclic LY-18). Dirty keys use Layout's encoding `(KIND << 32) | id`, `BODY` 2 (the shared family) and a new `ACT` 4, with **explicit dirty marking in every mutator** (4.7 packed-array element writes no longer call the property setter — verified-from-docs, `breaking-changes.md` 4.6 to 4.7, "Packed array element writes"). The full interface is in States and Transitions. *Decides:* R8, CR-9, LY-18; P1 (no half-applied weld leaves an actor in a frame that does not exist). (auto) → ADR-BODY-02.

182	**BDY-22 — Weld transfer (BM3).** On attach, only actors on the ABSORBED body are touched: `pos_curr += frame_shift_px`, `body_id := surviving_body_id`, `pos_prev := pos_curr`, `sub` and `last_octant` untouched (a whole-pixel shift cannot disturb a residue), and `BODY_TRANSFER{weld}` is emitted for those actors only. **Host-body actors are untouched** ("a weld moves nothing already built", LY:250). BM3 deletes the absorbed body's pose row. The mutator runs in P2 and `body.integrate` in P3 of the same tick, so the shifted actor is stepped this tick from the shifted position with a zero interpolation delta; the one-tick transfer artefact is removed by the Pipeline's C5 REBASE, not by Body: `BODY_TRANSFER{weld}` carries `frame_delta_px = +frame_shift_px` (3.7), and the Pipeline shifts its camera solver's `f` and history by it into the surviving body's frame and keeps the lag, so the avatar's screen position does not move (registry `camera_cut_predicates`: a weld or detach `BODY_TRANSFER` that carries `frame_delta_px` is a rebase, not a cut); a hard cut, never a pan, happens only where the new body's camera bounds clamp the rebased target *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. `frame_shift_px` is Layout's return value (the absorbed frame's origin expressed in the host frame, LY D.6; airlock fixture `(576, 96)`); Assembly passes the home-ship socket first, so the home-ship's body survives (LY-16, LY OQ-21). The invariant that makes this safe, stated as a test: for every actor moved, `(actor_section, actor_local_px)` is identical before and after (BDY-29). *Decides:* R7, LY-16; T3. (auto: D.4 fixture)

184	**BDY-23 — Detach transfer (BM4): the foot origin picks the side.** For each actor on the old body the side is the component whose section contains the foot ORIGIN on the detach tick (PCI:651, PCI:1001); a foot box straddling the seam is not split. Because BM4 runs after Layout's mutator, Layout has already re-based the moved sections, so Body evaluates containment against the **reconstructed pre-cut geometry**: for `s` in `moved_sections[]`, `offset_pre(s) = section_offset(s) + frame_shift_px`; for every other section of the old body `offset_pre(s) = section_offset(s)` (D.5; stated once as the call-order trap). Containment is by the section's FLOOR area (its rooms and the rectangles it owns, including its own 24-px hull footprint and hatch rectangles), never by bounding box, because hull-abutting sections have overlapping bounding boxes. Actors on `C_new`: `pos_curr -= frame_shift_px`, `body_id := new_body_id`, `pos_prev := pos_curr`, `sub := (0, 0)`, `last_octant` kept (harmless: `sub` is already zero, so a held key reads "no change"); emit `BODY_TRANSFER{detach}` with `frame_delta_px = -frame_shift_px` (3.7) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. Actors on `C_keep` are untouched. An origin lying in no section (an exterior gap, a defect) stays on `C_keep` and counts `BDY_TRANSFER_NO_SECTION`; this is a defect-only state, CI asserts it never occurs in a clean build (AC-BDY-29a), and its consequence is exterior exposure, never the last room's atmosphere (BDY-29, 8.3). BM4 creates the new body's pose row from the old body's (`world := world_old + frame_shift_px`, `vel := vel_old`, plus the default-zero detach drift of BDY-28), so a cut leaves both halves co-moving; *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **the new row is always restorable.** The pose range is a restore rule (`BDY_RESTORE_POSE_RANGE`), so a BM4 that wrote an out-of-range row would make the next autosave unloadable and break BDY-21's `restore(snapshot())` guarantee and the death-restart path. The normal defence is `can_rebase_detach`'s `BDY_REBASE_POSE_OUT_OF_RANGE` and `BDY_VEL_OUT_OF_RANGE` (BDY-21) and Transit's re-origin discipline (WM-6 keeps every pose within `WEB_COORD_BUDGET_PX`, 1/32 of the limit). The apply-time net for a caller that ignored the read is the D.7 freeze rule applied to the new row: if `world_old + frame_shift_px` leaves the range the new `world` is saturated per axis to `±WORLD_COORD_LIMIT` and `vel` is set to `(0, 0)`; if `vel_old + drift` leaves `±VEL_MAX_PX_PER_TICK` it is saturated per axis; `BDY_WORLD_LIMIT` (where applicable) and `BDY_PLAN_MISMATCH` count through the sink and BM4 returns `OK`: this is the saturate-and-continue class of BDY-21, and every other BM4 defect returns its `FAULT_CODE` and writes nothing *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. This is the one place a stored coordinate is saturated, it is defect-only, it touches the exterior pose alone (the interior bytes are unchanged, BDY-2), and the exterior `abs` conservation below is waived on that branch; the Controller clears `channel_ref` and keeps `octant`, `carry_ref` and `facing` (its rule, cited). The `sub` zeroing is a TRANSFER rule and does not conflict with BDY-31 (a restore is not a transfer). **Conservation law (the spike's falsifiable invariant):** with `abs(actor) = world(body_of(actor)) + pos_curr(actor)`, detach conserves `abs` exactly for every actor on either side; a weld conserves `abs` iff the docking invariant of BDY-27 holds; and **a weld followed by a cut of the same seam is not in general an identity on `pos_curr`** (detach re-bases to the section `m` with minimum id in `C_new`, LY D.12, while a weld shifts by the absorbed offset; the two coincide only when the absorbed body's section sat at its own frame origin), so any round-trip criterion asserts `abs` and the section-local position, never raw `pos_curr`. Fixture: Layout `fixture_chain` (chain 1 `(0, 0)`, 3 `(576, 96)`, 4 `(1056, 96)` cut at the (1, 3) seam: `frame_shift_px (576, 96)`, new offsets 3 `(0, 0)`, 4 `(480, 0)`). *Decides:* R7, LY-17, PCI:651; T3. (auto: D.5 fixture)

186	**BDY-24 — The hatch-cap hazard: refuse on player origin, never displace.** After a cut the socket's hatch is a SOLID `HULL` rectangle (`CAPPED` or `CUT_OPEN`, LY-15), so an actor standing in the hatch passage ends inside a footprint — a real hazard no designed GDD names. (i) Body publishes the pure read `actors_overlapping(body_id, rects[]) -> actor_id[]` (ascending); Assembly's `validate` of a PLAYER-origin cut rejects while it is non-empty for the seam's two hatch rectangles (the reason code is Assembly's: `MSA.CUT_BLOCKED`, adopted in MSA-21). **Origin is read as Assembly's `cause`** (consistency pass 2026-10-27, routed from `modular-ship-assembly.md` C7): hooks submit SYSTEM-origin commands only (KRN CR-3), so every channel-completed cut reaches P2 as SYSTEM-origin; throughout this GDD "PLAYER-origin cut" means `seam_cut {cause CHANNEL}` (rejects, at begin, handoff and completion) and "SYSTEM-origin cut" means `seam_cut {cause CASCADE}` (defers, MSA-22). (ii) If any transfer nonetheless lands an actor's foot box inside a SOLID rectangle — a system-origin cut, a restore of an older save, a template defect — BDY-16 applies: the body is never displaced. PCI:650 already rules the door analogue (a system-origin close enters `CLOSING_BLOCKED` and retries); this GDD turns the mirror into a **named must-repeat for Modular Ship Assembly (now Designed and repeating it, MSA-21, MSA-22; recorded in 8.3) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: was "provisional, undesigned")***: a SYSTEM-origin cut DEFERS while `actors_overlapping` is non-empty for the seam's two hatch rectangles, and the cut is preceded by the Pillar 2 tell window that Assembly and Adaptive Audio own (the 10 to 30 s escalating tell; the Graph's `W_MIN_WARNING_S` fairness gate), so a breach-driven cut can never separate a crewmate or seal one into a cap without a telegraphed window. How long a deferred cut may wait, and what Assembly does when the window expires with a crewmate still in the passage, are Assembly's (Open Question 10); Body supplies only the pure read. The no-displacement rule is unchanged and correct: the deferral prevents the overlap, it does not resolve one. **Struck:** a defensive deterministic push-out and its diagnostic, which contradict PCI:650 and P2. *Decides:* R7, LY-11, PCI:650, P2. (auto: hatch-cap fixture)

Body does not search for a free arrival cell (that would be a displacement): `can_transfer` answers `BDY_PLACE_INSIDE_FOOTPRINT` to the caller and Transit owns the alternative cell; two crewmates arriving at one cell is legal (BDY-17). **The pod is a Layout body** (Web Map & Transit is Designed and repeats it, WM-5 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: was "provisional — Web Map & Transit undesigned")*; Derelict Authoring DA-3 authors the `pod` template, one room `pod_cabin`, seat cell (72, 48)): a section built by Layout `build_section` from a pod template, with its own Layout `body_id`, counted against `MAX_BODIES`; Body places the actor on it. Uniform rectangle and occluder paths and the Emitter's `body_id` partition (EM-30) and Lighting's mask bits then work unchanged. Web Map & Transit must repeat (DA-3 already does): the pod template exists and the pod is a body. **Web Map's answer to SE-35 (consistency pass 2026-10-27; WM-5, WM-17):** `room_at` answers `pod_cabin`, never NONE, on the pod (consistent with BDY-29: NONE is never a place on a Layout body); the pod's air is Suit's `HOLD_ROOM` keyed on `loco_state == IN_POD` (WM-17, Web Map ASK-S1), not a NONE answer. *Decides:* R15, PCI:173, PCI:192, PCI:694, EM-30. 190	#### 1.5 Pose in the exterior frame, the inertial interior
191	
192	**BDY-26 — World pose, velocity and range.** `world_x`, `world_y` are integer base px that locate **the body-frame origin** (Layout's frame origin for that `body_id`, LY-3 (b)) in the exterior frame; `vel_x`, `vel_y` are whole base px per tick (no sub-pixel exterior residue in schema v1: the exterior layer is presentation and may interpolate by `tick_alpha`; a slower drift would be a schema bump made deliberately). `body.integrate` adds `vel` to `world` once per tick before stepping actors (BDY-9). Ranges: `|world_*| <= WORLD_COORD_LIMIT` 2^22 and `|vel_*| <= VEL_MAX_PX_PER_TICK` 16, both Body-registered `[PLACEHOLDER]`; `can_set_velocity` rejects `BDY_VEL_UNKNOWN_BODY` and `BDY_VEL_OUT_OF_RANGE`; the defence against a leg that would run past the world range is the `BDY_WORLD_LIMIT` freeze of BDY-9 (a mis-scripted leg is Transit's lint, not a Body projection); the 2^22 bound exists so a canvas offset (a difference of two world coordinates, within ±2^23) stays inside the range a float32 `Node2D.position` represents exactly (2^24) **[UNV: build precision]** (→ ADR-BODY-03). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Lowering either bound is a schema bump.** `BDY_RESTORE_POSE_RANGE` rejects any saved row beyond the CURRENT `WORLD_COORD_LIMIT` or `VEL_MAX_PX_PER_TICK`, so lowering either constant after saves exist makes those saves unloadable; a lowering therefore ships with `schema_version` 2 and a migration that saturates the stored rows (Save/Load's migration, SL), never as a silent tuning change. The defaults stay 2^22 and 16: Web Map & Transit's own budget is stated against them (`WEB_COORD_BUDGET_PX` 2^17 `<= WORLD_COORD_LIMIT / 32`, WM L741/L953), so a 2^21 default would break a designed neighbour's lint (declined, Open Question 35). **Derived exterior interpolation state (not persisted, not hashed, not replicated).** The exterior layer interpolates by `tick_alpha` (the one interpolator), so the read view carries `world_prev(body_id)`: the pose one tick ago. It is set `:= world` immediately before `body.integrate` adds `vel` (BDY-9), and **reset to the new `world` on every discontinuous write**: BM7 `set_body_pose` (including a Transit re-origin), BM4 for the new body's row, `post_restore` for every row, a BM6 that deletes a sparse row, and the BDY-9 freeze. BM3 deletes the absorbed row and writes none. A reset gives a stall of at most one tick of `vel` (at most 16 px, once) in place of a smear across the discontinuity. The renderer reads `canvas_offset_render(b, tick_alpha) = floor(off_prev + (off_curr - off_prev) * tick_alpha)` per axis, with `off_curr = world(b) - world(avatar_body)` and `off_prev = world_prev(b) - world_prev(avatar_body)` (D.7); the CURRENT avatar body is used for both, so a BM5 origin switch (the avatar's body changes on a pod hop, a weld or a cut) never interpolates across two reference frames — the Pipeline's C5 rebase (weld, cut) or cut (pod hop) fires on the same `BODY_TRANSFER` and the first post-switch frame has `off_prev` relative to the new origin *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. **`heading_q` is reserved and MUST be 0**, and is rejected on restore with `BDY_RESTORE_HEADING_UNSUPPORTED` (the mirror of Layout's `rot_q` and `LAYOUT_ROT_UNSUPPORTED`, LY:154); a tumbling hulk is an exterior-layer sprite, never a simulation fact. 206	**BDY-32 — Determinism contract (G3 and G4).** (1) *Order:* actors in ascending `actor_id`, bodies in ascending `body_id`, pose before actors; actors cannot affect one another (BDY-17), so actor order cannot change a result, yet it is fixed so that diagnostics and dirty-key insertion are reproducible. 525	### D.9 Interior invariance
526	
527	The interior invariance formula is defined as:
528	
529	`for all ticks t:   H_actors( t | vel = v, world = w )  ==  H_actors( t | vel = 0, world = 0 )   for every admissible (v, w)`
530	
531	Equivalently, the interior view is a function with no argument in the `bodies` table: `interior_view(actors, layout.state)`. This is the registered rule `interior_invariance`.
532	
533	**Variables:**
534	
535	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
536	|---|---|---|---|---|
537	| `H_actors` | bytes | canonical bytes of the `actors` table (BDY-32 order) | the kernel's `state_hash` (kernel D.12), compared per table | the actor table's contribution to the hash |
538	| `v`, `w` | int pairs | D.7 ranges | the acceptance fixture | any admissible exterior velocity and pose |
539	
540	**Output Range:** equality at every tick. The whole-block `state_hash` of `body.state` differs when `world_*` or `vel_*` differ, BY DESIGN (the `bodies` rows are part of the block); a criterion written against the whole-block hash would fail falsely, so the criterion compares the actor-table contribution (and `layout.state`).
541	
542	**Example (acceptance fixture):** give the avatar's body `vel = (3, 0)`, run 600 ticks of a scripted command stream, and run the identical stream at `vel = (0, 0)`: the `actors` bytes match at every tick, while the `bodies` row differs by `world.x = 1,800` at tick 600. A lint asserts that nothing reachable from `solid_in`, the actor loop of `body.integrate`, the Emitter, Suit or the interior camera pose names `world_` or `vel_`.
543	
544	### D.10 Section lookup
545	
546	The section lookup formula is defined as:
547	
548	`actor_section(a) = s  iff  pos_curr(a) in cells(s) + section_offset(s),  s in sections_of(body_id(a));   NONE otherwise;     actor_local_px(a) = pos_curr(a) - section_offset(actor_section(a))`
549	
550	**Containment, not precedence (CP-5).** `cells(s)` is each section's own half-open cell set (its rooms and the rectangles it owns, LY-7); LY-14's `GEOM_OVERLAP` test on every rect pair of a mate and the LY:207 `RECT_OVERLAP` lint make those sets disjoint across sections, so a point lies in at most one section and no tie rule exists or is needed.
551	
552	**Variables:**
553	
554	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
555	|---|---|---|---|---|
556	| `pos_curr(a)` | int pair | body frame | `body.state` | the foot ORIGIN (box top-centre) decides, not the box |
557	| `cells(s)` | half-open cell set, section-local | rooms plus owned rectangles, incl. the 24-px hull footprint and hatch rectangles | Layout template (*(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* Layout's `section_at(body_id, px)` (LY-28) publishes exactly this containment and is what Body calls; Body keeps no scan fallback, BDY-29) | the section's floor area |
558	| `section_offset(s)` | int pair | on the 24-px grid, may be negative after a detach | Layout | body-frame section origin |
559	
560	**Output Range:** a section id or NONE; derived on demand at call time, never stored, any cache invalidated by every mutator and every restore (BDY-29). `actor_local_px` is SECTION-LOCAL (negative only if the geometry says so); Layout's `room_at(section_id, px)` takes it (LY-3 (c)) and floors (LY-3 (f)).
561	
562	**Example (`LY D.6` airlock, sections 1 at `(0, 0)` and 3 at `(576, 96)`; A's east wall plate `[672, 696) x [240, 336)`, B's west wall plate `[696, 720) x [240, 336)` in body cells):** an origin at `(695, 280)` lies in `[672, 696)`, so section 1, `actor_local_px = (695, 280)`; an origin at `(696, 280)` lies in `[696, 720)`, so section 3, `actor_local_px = (696 - 576, 280 - 96) = (120, 184)`. That `x = 696` belongs to B is a consequence of half-open rectangles, not a rule. An origin in an exterior gap of the body answers NONE, a defect-only state whose consequence is exterior exposure (BDY-29, 8.3), never the last room's air.
563	
564	### D.11 Overlap exemption and `actors_overlapping`
565	
566	The overlap exemption formula is defined as:
567	
568	`ov(box, r) = max(0, min(box.x1, r.x1) - max(box.x0, r.x0)) * max(0, min(box.y1, r.y1) - max(box.y0, r.y0));     E = { r SOLID : ov(foot_box(pos_start), r) > 0 }  (fixed for the tick);     a 1-px sub-step to box_after is admitted  iff  for every r in E:  ov(box_after, r) <= ov(box_before, r)`

569	
570	Every rectangle not in `E` stays fully solid, so an exempt actor cannot walk into a wall it was not already inside. The test is **per rectangle, not total** (CP-1): on the `fixture_airlock` hull-line geometry a box astride two abutting exempt rectangles keeps its TOTAL overlap while stepping across their shared edge, which a total-area test would admit and the per-rectangle test refuses. Nothing shoves: `pos` is unchanged on every tick the actor does not step.
571	
572	**Variables:**
573	
574	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
575	|---|---|---|---|---|
576	| `box`, `box_before`, `box_after` | half-open rect | D.2 | `foot_box` at the sub-step | the foot box before and after one 1-px sub-step on either axis |
577	| `r` | half-open rect | body frame | Layout's `solid_in` result (SOLID filter) | a candidate rectangle |
578	| `ov(box, r)` | int | 0 to `FOOT_BOX_W * FOOT_BOX_H` = 128 | calculated | overlapped cells |
579	| `E` | set of rectangles | 0 to `K` (D.12) | calculated at the start of the actor's tick | rectangles the start box already intersects; empty on every ordinary tick |
580	
581	**Output Range:** `E` empty means ordinary sweeping. For a PARTIAL overlap any sub-step with a component away from a rectangle shrinks that rectangle's `ov`, so the box leaves in a bounded number of ticks and can never deepen. A sub-step is also refused when its destination foot origin lies in no section of the actor's body (D.10), so no exempt step leaves the hull. Residuals (defect-only, BDY-16): a box wholly inside one rectangle has constant `ov` until an edge crosses out (it may exit either side provided the destination origin is in a section of the body); a box astride two abutting exempt rectangles can only slide along the shared edge or back out; a hatch-cap actor whose only shrinking direction leaves the body cannot leave (the cap trap). Each actor-tick on which `E` is evaluated non-empty (plus each detection event that finds `E` non-empty) increments `PC_FOOTPRINT_OVERLAP` (BDY-16 counting rule) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Exposure of a footprint-resident exempt actor (stated once in BDY-16, repeated in BDY-29):** an exempt actor whose origin is inside a wall or hull-plate footprint of its own body has a section (`actor_section != NONE`) but `room_at(section, local)` answers NONE (Layout, LY-5), and Suit maps that to EXPOSED (SE:342); the guarantee is visibility, not safety, and a door-leaf exemption answers `sill_room` and is not exposed.
582	
583	**Example (BDY-16 hatch cap, after a SYSTEM-origin cut):** `pos = (690, 282)`, box `[682, 698) x [282, 290)`, plate `[672, 696) x [240, 336)`: `ov = (696 - 682) * 8 = 112`. West (box `[681, 697)`): `ov = 15 * 8 = 120 > 112`, refused. East (box `[683, 699)`): `13 * 8 = 104`, admitted. North or south: `14 * 8 = 112`, admitted. Walking east at `V_WALK` 2 the actor reaches `pos.x = 695` (692, 694, 695 over three ticks) and stops: the sub-step to 696 passes the overlap test (`ov` 64) but its destination origin `(696, 282)` lies in plate B's footprint, which left with its section and is in no section of this body, so exit containment refuses it. The actor rests in the cap at `pos.x = 695` (`ov = 72`), `actor_section` still answers section 1, and `PC_FOOTPRINT_OVERLAP` counts every tick on which it presses a key (the cap trap; the exit it would have taken is the exterior face). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **At that resting pose `room_at(1, (695, 282))` answers NONE (inside plate A's footprint), so Suit reads EXPOSED: vacuum, anoxic, exterior temperature, on a pressurised ship.** This is the accepted residual, not a safe state (BDY-16). **The trap region is a strip, not the single point 695:** with box `[x - 8, x + 8) x [y, y + 8)` and plate `[672, 696) x [240, 336)`, the box straddles the plate's east edge for `x` 689 to 695 (at `x = 689`, box `[681, 697)`, `ov = 15 * 8 = 120`; west gives `[680, 696)`, `ov = 128`, refused; east gives `ov = 112`, admitted); for `x` 680 to 688 the box lies wholly inside the plate (`ov` constant at 128), west is admitted and the actor can walk back onto the floor, so those starts are residual (i), not the trap. In `y` the strip is `y` 240 to 328 (box rows wholly inside the plate's rows); at `y` 233 to 239 and 329 to 335 the neighbouring hull-wall rectangle joins `E` and the outcome depends on Layout's neighbour geometry, which the fixture does not fix. **Admitted-move set for each direction at `pos = (690, 282)`** (fixture assumption: the hull-wall footprint rectangles continue north and south of the plate and are not in `E` at the start): **east** is admitted for sub-steps to `x` 691 to 695 and refused at 696 (exit containment); **west** is refused at once (`ov` 120 > 112); **north** and **south** are admitted by the overlap test (`ov` stays 112) while the box rows stay inside `[240, 336)`, that is down to `y = 240` (north) and `y = 328` (south), and are refused at 239 and 329 by the non-`E` neighbour rectangles; an **east** input from anywhere in the strip converges to `x = 695`, a **north-east** input converges to `(695, 240)`, a **south-east** input to `(695, 328)`. The criterion asserts this full set (AC-BDY-29). **Abutting case:** `pos = (696, 282)` with both plates `[672, 696)` and `[696, 720)` in `E`: `ov_A = 8 * 8 = 64`, `ov_B = 64`, total 128. East (box `[689, 705)`): `ov_A = 56`, `ov_B = 72 > 64`, refused although the total is 128 again; west is refused symmetrically; north and south (both stay 64) are admitted.
584	
585	The actors-overlapping formula is defined as:
586	
587	`actors_overlapping(body_id, rects[]) = { a on body_id :  there exists r in rects with ov(foot_box(pos_curr(a)), r) > 0 },  in ascending actor_id`
588	
589	The pure read Assembly's `validate` of a PLAYER-origin (`cause CHANNEL`) cut calls with the seam's two hatch rectangles (BDY-24); non-empty means reject (the reason code is Assembly's, `MSA.CUT_BLOCKED`).
590	
591	**Variables:**
592	
593	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
594	|---|---|---|---|---|
595	| `rects[]` | list of half-open rects, body frame | the seam's two hatch rectangles, each `width_tiles * 48` by 24 (LY-15) | Assembly, from Layout | the rectangles the cut would cap |
596	| `pos_curr(a)` | int pair | body frame | `body.state` at the tick the command validates | tick-start position |
597	
598	**Output Range:** an ascending list of `actor_id`; empty means the cut may proceed. **Example:** hatch plates `[672, 696) x [240, 336)` and `[696, 720) x [240, 336)`; an actor at `pos = (690, 282)` has box `[682, 698) x [282, 290)`: `ov` with the first 112 and with the second `(698 - 696) * 8 = 16`, both positive, so the list holds that actor and the player cut is rejected; an actor at `pos = (640, 250)` has box `[632, 648)`, no overlap, and the list is empty. A multi-tick cut channel re-validates on its completion tick (a single-tick command cannot be raced because Assembly's `apply` is atomic in one P2, KRN:197).

21	## Overview
22	
23	**The framing conflict, stated first.** The systems index describes this system as "the composite ship as one physics body with a ship-local reference frame; characters and props moving inside a moving body (the moving-platform problem); detach spawns a new body" (IDX:29). Read as a mandate to build an engine physics body per ship, that sentence is wrong for this game, and four designed GDDs have already removed engine physics from it: the Controller says "the avatar has no physics body" and moves it by a hand-rolled integer `LocomotionStep` (PCI:103, PC-14 PCI:143); Layout's rectangles are simulation data "never produced by an engine physics shape" and its projector builds no engine tile collision and no navigation mesh in the MVP (LY-7, LY-31); the Emitter's occlusion is an integer segment-versus-rectangle test and "physics-derived observations never enter this block" (EM-30); and the Pipeline draws the interior in the avatar's body frame at the canvas origin, where "ship motion through the void never appears in the interior view" and "ship rotation is never rendered inside" (PIPE C2). The consequence, which this GDD adopts as its first rule (BDY-2, BDY-3): **in the MVP the moving-platform problem is a data problem, not an engine problem.** Every actor's position is an integer in its body's own frame; the composite welded ship is ONE body because Layout holds exactly one `body_id` per welded set (LY-18); a body that moves through the exterior therefore cannot move anything standing inside it, and a weld, a cut or a pod hop is integer arithmetic on stored positions. *(orchestrator ruling R1: option (a), an integer kinematic frame with a pose-invariant interior; options (b) one engine rigid body per ship and (c) an engine-physics exterior hybrid are rejected, the second surviving only as the presentation-only ADR-BODY-05 candidate.)*
24	
25	**What it is, in one sentence.** Ship Body & Interior Physics is the single owner of *where each actor is inside its body* and *how each body sits in the exterior frame*: a scene-tree-free, integer-only `SIM` block (`body.state`) that holds every actor's body-frame kinematic state and every body's sparse pose and velocity, one per-tick hook (`body.integrate`) that runs the pure `LocomotionStep` sweep against Layout's rectangles, seven mutators that re-home actors when Assembly welds, cuts or Transit hops a pod, or set a body's exterior velocity or pose, a handful of pure reads, and one `PROJECTOR` subscriber that owns the per-body scene root and the camera-limit rectangle. Layout owns the geometry and the `body_id`; the Controller owns intent, octant, gait and the chest point; the Pipeline owns frame composition; Assembly and Transit own the commands that move actors between bodies. Body owns the one thing none of them do: the integer position of a person on a deck, and the arithmetic that keeps it true when the deck is joined to another or cut in two.
26	
27	**Who owns what (closes the kernel's and the Controller's open boundary).** *Ship Body owns ship-local integer position* — `pos_curr`, `sub`, `last_octant`, `odometer`, `blocked`, the foot box, the sweep, the body transfers and the `LocomotionStep` — *and the Controller owns intent, octant, gait, `v_eff`, committed aim, facing, locomotion state, carry and channel references, the chest point and the hand point.* This closes kernel Open Question 3 (KRN:194, KRN:958) and the Controller's PC-14 recommendation (PCI:143, PCI:1108), which both asked for exactly this split. Body reads `octant` and `v_eff` from `controller.state` and derives nothing of the Controller's (BDY-11). The lamp is **chest**-mounted and hands-free (user decision): if this GDD names a beam origin at all it is the chest point, which the Controller publishes; the foot origin Body owns is the shadow and occluder origin (LO-10); the hand point is a lightless tool grip and nothing in Body touches it.
28	
29	**How the player meets it.** Never as a menu, a gauge, a velocity readout or a mechanic. The player meets Body as *footing*: a deck that stops exactly where the 24-px wall footprint says it stops (`WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH`), a stop that is pixel-exact with no overshoot, a wall that is slid along rather than stuck to, and — at the two moments the game is most violent on paper — a weld and a cut during which nothing at all happens to the floor under their boots. Ship motion, docking contact and hull separation are events out in the exterior layer and the sound of the hull; they are never forces on the interior (BDY-28). The only things the player *does* that reach Body are walking and the Assembly and Transit verbs that Body's mutators serve, and each lands in `body.state` as an atomic, replayable change.
30	
31	**What the game loses without it.** Nothing else owns the integer position of a person on a deck. Without Body, `LocomotionStep` has no home and the Controller's 12 sweep tests (PC-18) have no module; Suit's room lookup (SE-3) has no `section_id` to supply; the Emitter's ACTOR anchor (EM-21) and the lamp's shadow origin (LO-10) have no `pos_curr` to read, and `emitter.state`'s `restore_after: [layout.state, graph.state, body.state, controller.state]` (EM-1) names a block that does not exist, which fails boot; Save/Load's mandatory set (SL:288) has no `body.state` and the kernel's restore-idempotence debt (`REBASE_BLOCKS`, SL:577) stays open; a weld or cut would leave every actor standing in a frame that no longer exists; and the weld spike — the riskiest MVP task, the reason this system was added to the index as a `TD-SYSTEM-BOUNDARY` addition (IDX:65, IDX:276) — would have no owner for "the motion". Because the spike is *weld on a moving ship*, the GDD's answer is that welding is safe by construction: weld legality takes no pose input (BDY-27), and the interior never reads the pose.
32	
33	**Scope guard: what Body does not own.** Geometry, `body_id` allocation, membership, offsets, welds, sockets, seams, hatch states and door leaves are Layout's (LY-18, LY-35); Body owns *pose and actors only*. **No prop is a Body actor in the MVP** (BDY-4): loose items are Interaction records in section-local pixels, so "a weld or a detach moves nothing" (IA-28, LY-22); static props and machinery are Layout rectangles; a thrown glowstick lands by an analytic rule (IA-29); a horror's footprint is a Graph trail, never a Body fact. The index's word "props" is therefore satisfied by a statement, not a mechanism; a Vertical Slice movable prop adds one `kind` here and one bump-list entry in Layout deliberately (LY:229). Intent, gait and the chest point belong to the Controller; camera, zoom, the cut rule and the exterior/transit layers to the Pipeline; weld and cut commands, weld quality `q` and the order of mutators to Assembly and the Graph; the loaded set, the pod leg and the docking script to Web Map & Transit; atmosphere and damage to the Life-Support Graph; sanity and perceived values to Sanity and the Perception Filter. There is no HUD element, no overlay and no number that the player reads from Body. **MVP slice.** In: SEAT actors only (one seat, `MAX_ACTORS` 8); `LocomotionStep` and the sweep; BM1–BM7; weld (BM3) and cut (BM4) on the home-ship 5 / derelict A 4 / derelict B 5 compartment slice; *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings, X1: the weld, the player seam cut and the install are all MVP, so BM3 and BM4 serving a player-initiated cut carry no cut-first status; co-op stays out of the MVP)* the pod hop (BM5) and a constant-velocity pod leg (BM6); restore idempotence; `body.projector` with rotation 0. Later (Vertical Slice): AGENT rows for horrors (if Horror picks that path), `DETACH_DRIFT_PX_PER_TICK` > 0, sub-pixel exterior velocity, cross-body light, co-op replication (VS-B), presentation-only debris (ADR-BODY-05), actor soft separation.
34	
35	**Noun guard.** In concept prose "a body they assembled" means the composite ship. In this GDD **`body` / `body_id` is the rigid frame of a welded set** — Layout's id (LY-18), the thing that has a pose — and **"the avatar" or "an actor" is the person standing in it**. Internal nouns (`body`, `body_id`, `pos_curr`, frame, pose, velocity, transfer) are correct in rules and formulas and are never what the player experiences (see Player Fantasy, Language). The word "body" never becomes flesh: flesh tones and violet are reserved for sanity leaks (P1 sane palette), so no Body-originated cue may use them.
36	
37	**Engine statement (which 2D physics path this relies on).** *None.* The only 2D physics server in Godot 4.7.2 is Godot Physics 2D — **verified-from-docs**: `docs/engine-reference/godot/modules/physics.md` (4.6 changes) records "2D physics UNCHANGED (still Godot Physics 2D)", and `VERSION.md` shows Jolt as the 3D default since 4.6, which does not apply to 2D. Body uses that server for nothing on any simulation-authoritative path (BDY-3). The single candidate use is presentation-only debris at Vertical Slice (ADR-BODY-05), excluded from the simulation hash set (`ALL_SIM`). Because nothing is sampled from a physics step, the kernel's determinism limit G3 ("Godot Physics 2D makes no determinism claim, so G3 either records and replays [physics results] or excludes physics-coupled blocks", KRN:123, CR-13) is met by construction: `body.state` is a pure function of the command stream and Layout, kernel Open Question 5 is moot for the MVP, and the kernel row "hook sampling physics results into its block each tick" (KRN:198) collapses to `body.integrate` with nothing sampled (wording note routed in Cross-References). Everything this GDD says about `_physics_process` ordering, 2D interpolation, `TileMapLayer`, `Node.reparent`, GDScript integer-division semantics and canvas float precision is **[UNV]**: the engine reference has no `scripting.md`, `core.md`, `2d.md` or `tilemap.md` (its `modules/` holds animation, audio, input, navigation, networking, physics, rendering and ui only), and those claims are routed to the weld and motion spikes. Post-cutoff claims used here are tagged verified-from-docs against `breaking-changes.md` (4.6 to 4.7 packed-array element writes no longer call the property setter; typed-return overrides need an explicit `return` on every path).
38	
39	**Index wording, reconciled.** "The composite ship as one physics body with a ship-local reference frame" = one `body_id` per welded set (Layout) plus one sparse pose row per `body_id` (Body), where the *ship-local frame* is Layout's body frame (LY-3 (b)) and the frame's origin is the point Body locates in the exterior frame. "Characters and props moving inside a moving body (the moving-platform problem)" = BDY-2: positions are body-frame integers and nothing keyed on one reads the pose; props: BDY-4. "Detach spawns a new body" = Layout allocates the new `body_id` and returns `{new_body_id, moved_sections[], frame_shift_px}` (LY-17); Body creates the pose row from the old body's and re-homes the actors on the new side (BDY-23). "Physics PROJECTOR" (KRN:198) = `body.projector`, which builds nothing physical (BDY-33).
40	
41	*Implementation questions raised while designing and deferred to ADRs (→ `/architecture-decision`): the motion model and sweep formulation, hand-rolled integer kinematics against any engine body (ADR-BODY-01); the `body.state` shape, the persisted-versus-derived split and restore idempotence (ADR-BODY-02); the scene projection of a body, reparent-on-weld against rebuild, shared with ADR-LAY-03, and the camera-limit rectangle (ADR-BODY-03); the tick source and interpolation clock, shared with the kernel's tick ADR (ADR-BODY-04); and whether presentation-only debris may use engine physics at Vertical Slice (ADR-BODY-05).*
42	
43	## Player Fantasy
44	
45	**Framing: indirect.** The player never sees a body, a frame, a pose, a velocity or a transfer; they stand on what Body makes true. A direct framing would need a direct interaction, and the only candidates — steering the ship, bracing against it, physically shoving through it — are each forbidden below. *(creative-director consulted; three framings weighed and logged: **A "The Deck Is the Ground"** adopted as the headline; **B "Where Someone Is, Is Never a Lie"** adopted as its Pillar 4 guarantee rather than a competing headline, because the Controller already owns "a body tells the truth about its owner" (PCI:36) and Layout owns "The Wall Is the Last Witness" (LY:41); **C "The Helm"** rejected — nobody steers in the MVP, and a pilot fantasy breeds a helm, a velocity readout, inertia and brace mechanics, every one a violation of BDY-28.)* The structure mirrors Layout's headline-plus-guarantee so the two GDDs read as one promise from two sides: Layout says *the walls never move when you weld*; Body says *you never move when you weld*. Layout's own hand-off is honoured here: "you are standing where you stood" after a weld "is Body's and the Pipeline's to deliver, not a Layout rule" (LY:66).
46	
47	> Outside, the ship is a vehicle. It drifts along a strand of the web, takes wrecks onto itself and sheds them. Inside, it is the world. The floor does not tilt when the pod leaves, does not shudder when a wreck is welded to the hull, does not slide when half the ship is cut away. Whatever the web does to the ship, it does out there: on the hull, in the air, through the hatch, in the dark beyond a cap plate. It never does it to your footing. *(If the view ever shudders at a docking or a detach, that is the camera's `JOLT_PX`, the Pipeline's knob, default 0, forced to 0 by reduced motion, never the floor.)*
48	>
49	> That is why the weld and the cut are the quietest moments in the game. You are standing in a wreck's corridor when the weld finishes, and nothing happens to you. The same floor is under your boots, the same doorway is in front of your light; only now this corridor is part of your ship, and the crewmate on the other side of the seam is aboard with you. When a graft goes bad and the crew cuts it away, the half you are standing on is your ship. The crewmate who was standing past the seam is on the other half. Nobody was thrown, nobody stumbled; the gap between you is a fact you now have to deal with.
50	>
51	> And under Pillar 4, where someone is cannot be faked. A crewmate may look like a horror, sound wrong, carry a light you no longer trust; the place their feet are is the place their feet are, for every player, on every frame. When the shape lies, the position does not.
52	
53	**The emotion named: footing.** Not safety (the ship is never safe) and not control (the crew cannot steer it): the small, durable certainty that the ground under you is real and stays put, so that fear has to come from the world and can be read there. It is what makes the Pandorum ship-as-world credible — the void is unknowable precisely because the deck is not. MDA: Body's felt contribution is *Fantasy* ("we are the only ones awake"; a ship that is a world, not a vehicle) and *Challenge* as spatial certainty under pressure; *Fellowship* gains one concrete footing, the crewmate across a cut seam is truly *over there*. Body has no *Sensation* contribution of its own (see Visual/Audio and Game Feel). Body also deliberately contributes nothing to *Discovery*, the game's first-ranked aesthetic, and protects it only indirectly: a deck that never lies means every unknown the player investigates is in the world and not in their footing. This keeps the MDA mapping complete and stops a later revision from adding exploration mechanics (sea legs, traversal unlocks) to Body to "serve" rank 1; anti-pillar guard rail (6) below already forbids them.
54

76	| Live decision | Resolution | Rule |
77	|---|---|---|
78	| A transfer lands a foot box inside a SOLID rect | No push-out; the actor is never displaced and may only take sub-steps that do not deepen its overlap with any rectangle it already touches, and `PC_FOOTPRINT_OVERLAP` counts each such tick on which the exemption was evaluated *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: BDY-16 counting rule)* | BDY-16, PCI:650 |
79	| Ship acceleration, docking contact or detach acting on actors | None; published as events only, feeding `JOLT_PX` (default 0) and Adaptive Audio | BDY-28 |
80	| Rotation of a body rendered inside | Never; `heading_q` locked 0 | BDY-26, PIPE C2 |
81	| A perceived or per-player position | None | BDY-30 |
82	| `sub` zeroed on restore versus on transfer | Transfer and stop only; restore preserves it | BDY-12, BDY-31 |
83	| Player cut with a crewmate in the hatch passage | Refused by Assembly's `validate` via `actors_overlapping` | BDY-24 |
84	| System-origin cut (a breach cascade) with a crewmate in the hatch passage | Deferred by Assembly while `actors_overlapping` is non-empty, and preceded by the P2 tell window (a recorded must-repeat, 8.3); Body never displaces | BDY-24 |
85	| An exempt actor's step would put its foot origin in no section of its body | Refused: the only exits from a hatch cap lead back onto the body's own floor, never out of the hull. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* An actor that cannot leave a cap plate is visibly inside it and reads EXPOSED (Layout answers NONE inside a footprint): the guarantee is visibility, not safety | BDY-16, D.11 |
86	| Interior reads of world pose or velocity | Forbidden (lint plus an invariance test) | BDY-2 |
87	
88	*Secondary test (the P4 guarantee):* **a horror drawn where the crewmate is vs. a horror drawn somewhere the crewmate is not -> where the crewmate is.** It resolves BDY-30 and is a must-repeat for the Perception Filter (Designed, and it repeats BDY-30) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. *We will know this was right if* playtesters describe a weld as "suddenly we were connected" and a cut as "and then they were on the other side", never "the ship jerked" or "I got knocked"; and a code review finds no write to `pos_curr` outside `LocomotionStep` and the transfer arithmetic of BM1 to BM5.
89	
90	**How the fantasy deepens under hallucination (not breaks).**
91	
92	- **Class (a) phantom entities.** A phantom has no Body row (BDY-4: filter-only phantoms have none; a real horror holds its own position). What deepens: the player's own footing is never part of the lie, so "did I just get grabbed?" is answerable by the fact that nothing moved you — Body never moves an actor without a cause the simulation can show.
93	- **Class (b) false system states.** Geometry is outside the Filter's menu: Layout asks that wall faces, door leaves and seam geometry be tagged truth-channel (LY:41, LY:47; routed to the Perception Filter as a must-repeat). Body's sweep therefore never meets a hallucinated wall, and the player's body cannot be fooled about where it can walk or which side of a cut it is on. The class-(b) lies that remain — machine states, gauges, module sprites — have no Body share.
94	- **Class (c) crewmates as horrors.** Deepens most. The rig is driven by the crewmate's true `pos_curr` (Body) and true motion and beam (Controller, PCI:36, PCI:216); their beam rides their chest point. A player who watches where the "monster" stands and where its light comes from has a truth channel that costs attention, not certainty — and that is the channel on which system-gated lethal friendly harm is decided, so it must not lie.
95	- **Class (d) phantom salvage.** No Body share (Interaction and Item records, IA-28). Stated so no later rule makes carried weight a Body velocity effect: carry speed is the Controller's `V_CARRY`, not a Body modifier.
96	
97	Inherited guard rail from the Controller's secondary test ("-10% move speed vs. a gauge showing a false value -> the false gauge"): sanity never touches `body.state` — it never slows, shifts, drifts or displaces an actor.
98	
99	**Language (player-facing text and this section).** *Use:* deck, floor, underfoot, footing, aboard, over the seam, across the seam, the other half, adrift, the hop, the pod leg, your ship / their ship, the wreck, standing where you stood. *Never as player-facing nouns:* physics, physics body, inertia, momentum, g-force, gravity, lurch, jolt (as prose), shove, knockback, ragdoll, platform, moving platform, collider, hitbox, rigid body, frame / reference frame / transform / pose / velocity, teleport, snap.
100	
101	**Reference techniques — adopt and reject, precisely.**
102	
103	| Reference | Verdict | Exactly what |
104	|---|---|---|
105	| Pandorum | ADOPT | Ship-as-world: the interior is the whole world, the outside unknowable. The chest-mounted, hands-free lamp is the user's decision; the foot is the shadow and occluder origin; the hand point is lightless. |
106	| Beyond the Aquila Rift | ADOPT | A still, intimate interior against an incomprehensible exterior; the horror of distance (the other half, the void past a cap plate), not of violent motion. |
107	| Project Zomboid | ADOPT | A physics-free, pixel-stepped avatar whose position is a plain, exact fact; "death is a bitch. It happens." (user) without the floor ever being the killer. |
108	| Barotrauma | ADOPT the hull-is-world framing; REJECT ragdoll, sub-collision knockback and crew thrown by impacts | Its displacement is exactly the unannounced shove P2 forbids and a lethal-friendly-harm vector the anti-PvP anti-pillar forbids. |
109	| Sea of Thieves (visibly moving deck), FTL-style crew sliding with hull hits | REJECT | Interior motion breaks PIPE C2 and makes the floor an actor. |
110	| Space Engineers, Starbase (physical ships, per-block physics) | REJECT | The freeform-builder anti-pillar, and a physics body per ship contradicts BDY-3. |
111	| Dead Space zero-g sections, magnetic-boot gimmicks | REJECT | The interior is inertial and walking is the only locomotion (PC-12 lists what the player cannot do). |
112	| Stellaris | NOT APPLICABLE | Strategy-layer inspiration belongs to Web Map; nothing to adopt for Body. |
113	
114	**Anti-pillar guard rails this GDD states.** (1) *Not a combat game:* Body has no push, knockback, shove, impulse, ragdoll or stagger-from-motion, and nothing in Body can be used to displace another actor (PCI:139 PC-12). (2) *No intentional PvP:* Body offers no physical harm channel at all, sane or not, and adds no ungated one — crushing a crewmate in a cut is refused for player-origin cuts (BDY-24) and a system-origin overlap never displaces or damages (BDY-16); actors do not body-block one another (BDY-17), so no player can pin a crewmate in a corridor. (3) *Not a freeform builder:* no rotation (`heading_q` 0), no free placement, no dragging a section through space by the player; weld legality takes no pose input (BDY-27). (4) *No authored story, no win state:* no scripted interior motion, no authored "the ship lurches" moment. (5) *No meter:* no HUD element reads Body; no velocity, heading, g-force or docking-alignment readout. (6) *No progression:* no speed buff, traversal unlock or "sea legs".
115
